title: Mapping intestinal microenvironment heterogeneity in Hirschsprung's disease by spatial transcriptomics: Role of THBS1 in macrophage polarization and neural stem cell regulation

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Mapping intestinal microenvironment heterogeneity in Hirschsprung's disease by spatial transcriptomics: Role of THBS1 in macrophage polarization and neural stem cell regulation》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · p0010】Hirschsprung's disease (HSCR) is a congenital malformation of the digestive tract that is common in newborns. It is characterized by the complete or partial absence of ganglion cells in the colon.1,2 This pathological defect results in persistent spasmodic contractions in the affected intestinal segment, leading to excessive intestinal motility and distension of the proximal colon.3,4 While surgical resection of the ganglion cell-deficient segment remains the primary treatment, some patients develop postoperative complications, such as fecal incontinence or constipation.5,6 Therefore, further investigation into the pathogenesis of HSCR and the development of novel therapeutic strategies are urgently required.

【Introduction · p0015】HSCR primarily results from aberrant migration, survival, and differentiation of enteric neural crest cells. Current research indicates that mutations in genes such as Ret, Gdnf, Gfra1, Nrtn, Ednrb, Et3, Zfhx1b, Phox2b, and Sox10 account for approximately 50% of known HSCR cases.7, 8, 9 Beyond genetic factors, recent studies have shifted focus to the “gut microenvironment theory”, which emphasizes the regulatory roles of the extracellular matrix (ECM) and soluble factors in enteric neural crest cell development, with microenvironmental abnormalities potentially contributing to disease pathogenesis.10, 11, 12 Accordingly, the role of the gut microenvironment in HSCR pathogenesis has gained increasing attention.

【Clonal formation experiment · p0150】The SH-SY5Y cells were seeded at 1 × 103/well in six-well plates with three replicates. The medium was changed every 4 days. After 2 weeks, the cells were fixed with 4% polyformaldehyde for 15 min, stained with crystal violet for 15 min, washed, dried, and then photographed to count the clones.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Mapping intestinal microenvironment heterogeneity in Hirschsprung's disease by spatial transcriptomics: Role of THBS1 in macrophage polarization and neural stem cell regulation》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Cellular communication analysis · p0095】Addressing mixed-cell spots: To mitigate the impact of spots containing multiple cell types, we performed sensitivity analysis by repeating the communication analysis after excluding spots with high heterogeneity scores (entropy > 0.8). The major ligand–receptor pairs (including THBS1–SDC1) were consistent with the full analysis, supporting the robustness of the findings.

【General profiles of ST sequencing in HSCR · p0185】To identify cellular phenotypic characteristics among different subpopulations, we performed a bimodal marker gene analysis across the 18 subpopulations, identifying genes that were specifically expressed within each subpopulation (Fig. 1D). To evaluate the sensitivity of the ST method for detecting point transcripts, we examined the spatial distribution of marker genes for common cell types in previously reported samples.19, 20, 21 The results confirmed that Des and Flna (markers typically associated with smooth muscle cells) were highly expressed in the intrinsic muscle layer, Prph (a marker typically associated with gastrointestinal neuronal cells) was localized in the neural tissue region, and Ern2 (a marker typically associated with gastrointestinal epithelial cells) was expressed in the mucosal layer. Together, these findings validate the reliability of the ST sequencing results (Fig. 1E).

sections.title: 图表阅读

【Figure 6 · fig6】Figure 6 Expression of THBS1 in macrophages affects the proliferation, migration, and apoptosis of SH-SY5Y cells. (A) CCK8 assay for SH-SY5Y viability. (B) Colony-forming assay for SH-SY5Y proliferation. (C) Transwell assay for SH-SY5Y migration. Scale: 100 μm. (D) Cell scratch assay for SH-SY5Y migration. Scale: 200 μm. (E) Flow cytometry for SH-SY5Y apoptosis rate. ns: not statistically significant; ∗p < 0.05, ∗∗p < 0.01, ∗∗∗p < 0.001, and ∗∗∗∗p < 0.0001. Data shown are from non-contact Transwell co-culture experiments (0.4 μm pore size) as described in the methods. All experiments were performed in triplicate (n = 3 independent biological replicates). Data were expressed as mean ± standard deviation. Groups: CTRL (untreated control), siTHBS1+Vec (THBS1 knockdown with empty vector), siNC + oeTHBS1 (control siRNA with THBS1 overexpression), siTHBS1+oeTHBS1 (THBS1 knockdown with THBS1 overexpression, rescue group). Note that the rescue group showed partial but incomplete restoration of the phenotypes compared with the siNC + oeTHBS1 group, particularly in migration assays. Statistical significance was determined by one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post-hoc test. ∗p < 0.05, ∗∗p < 0.01, ∗∗∗p < 0.001, and ∗∗∗∗p < 0.0001; ns, not significant.

【Figure 1 · fig1】Figure 1 The spatial transcriptomic landscape of HSCR. (A) UMAP visualization of all points across 18 clusters (colored by cluster and spatial position). (B) Specific gene expression patterns and hematoxylin–eosin staining images for 18 clusters in sample space slices. Scale: 200 μm. (C) Proportional distribution of 18 clusters across different samples. (D) Gene expression profiles specific to 18 clusters. (E) Tissue-specific gene annotations across the eight tissues. Sample sizes: n = 3 HSCR patients (seven tissue segments) and n = 1 control (one segment).

【Figure 2 · fig2】Figure 2 Key gene atlas of extracellular matrix (ECM) regulating the enteric neural crest cells. (A) Expression of ECM-and immune cell-related genes within each cluster. (B) Volcano plots of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between the spastic and control groups. The DEGs were labeled. p-value < 0.05, Fold change > 1.2. (C) GO enrichment analysis and KEGG pathway analysis of the differentially expressed genes. (D) Violin plots of ECM-related genes in all clusters. The width of a violin plot indicates the kernel density of the expression values. (E) Correlation analyses on DEGs in the cluster with higher ECM scores. Sample sizes: spastic segments (n = 2), control segments (n = 1). Statistical significance for DEGs was determined by the Wilcoxon test with p < 0.05 and fold change > 1.2.
